subject: devtools build not filling man or R directories

messages.author: 9666dc9bc1163273
messages.subject: devtools build not filling man or R directories
parts:
Hello

I believe I've been following the given directions but I can not seem to create a package using devtools so I think I'm missing a critical step.  I'm using the latest versions of R and relevant packages.  I'm using a MacBook Pro (updated OSX10.11.2).

I begin with a directory (DevTTools) that has single file in it that contains two simple functions (mymin and mymax, simple calls to min and max functions).  Preceding both of these functions is the code to build the documentation.

At this point I setwd to the parent (DevTTools) and run build().   It seems to run correctly -- I'm not sure exactly what the output should be but I can see that the DESCRIPTION and NAMESPACE files are created as well as the R and man directories.  However, there's nothing in the R and man directories and the tar.gz file that is created also does not have anything in the R or man directories.   What am I missing?

In some of the devtools instructions, one is told to download Xcode.  I've done that but don't know how to use it, the instructions make little or no mention of what to do with it, and I am not seeing the connection between Xcode and devtools.  I'm thinking this might be part of my problem but I haven't found any instruction on this.





R Code for my test file:
#' My minimum
#'
#' Finds the minimum value within a vector of values in \code{\link{mymin}}
#'
#' @param vlist a vector of numbers
#'
#' @return a real number
#'
#' @examples
#' mymin(c(1,2,3,4,5))
#'
#' @export
#' mymin()
mymin <- function(vlist){
d <- min(vlist)
return(d)
}
#' My maximum
#'
#' Finds the maximum value within a vector of values in \code{\link{mymax}}
#'
#' @param vlist a vector of numbers
#'
#' @return a real number
#'
#' @examples
#' mymax(c(1,2,3,4,5))
#'
#' @export
#' mymax()
mymax <- function(vlist){
d <- max(vlist)
return(d)
}

shouldn't expect the contents of the built package to look exactly
that same as your source package.

Hadley

Thanks for your quick response.

Have I read the link?  Yes and no.  I am not using RStudio on my MacBook so most of it does not apply.  The instructions I have used do not specifically require or mention RStudio.  So, is RStudio required?

Also,  I have successfully created packages before (I have one on CRAN) but I built it "the hard way" using package.skeleton() and building / checking from the terminal.  My goal here is to do the same thing but use devtools.  It seems so much easier, but it is giving me no real output -- completely empty R and man directories.

JKreke
